## Problem

On the apply path, a model response that carries no `HARNESS_READY` marker is treated as a confident candidate — including when the response is not code at all (e.g. a safety-refusal string). The refusal class is not screened at intake, and the model is credited with a healthy result for it. Downstream gates caught the observed instance (zero bytes written), so this is intake hygiene + health-accounting correctness, not a breach — but the screening belongs at intake, where the other malformed-output classes are already handled.

Found during the 2026-10-20 full verification pass on main `dd83caf9`.

## Evidence (verified in code + observed live)

Intake flow:

- `harness/prompts.py:204-249` — `_parse_ready` returns `"missing"` when no marker is present. The treat-as-confident policy is deliberate and documented at `prompts.py:209-211` ("treat as confident with a warning so the verify gate + DEFER backstop still protect us").
- `harness/apply_policy.py:424` — `ready, ready_reason, content = _parse_ready(content)`.
- `harness/apply_policy.py:443-448` — the `ready == "missing"` branch logs `"did not emit HARNESS_READY; treating as confident (verify + DEFER still guard)"` and falls through with the raw content as the candidate.
- `harness/apply_policy.py:441-442` — the response is recorded billable with status `"ok"`, and at `apply_policy.py:458` `_note_model_health(attempt_model, ok=True)` credits the model's health — for a response that may be a refusal.
- `harness/prompts.py:178-200` — `_extract_file_content` then packages the response body as the new file content (no refusal/non-code screening anywhere in this path).
- Existing intake guards cover the neighboring classes correctly: empty content and reasoning-only responses (`REASONING_FALLBACK_PREFIX`) rotate with health `ok=False` at `harness/apply_policy.py:409-423`; an explicit `HARNESS_READY: defer` rotates at `apply_policy.py:426-440`. Refusal/non-code text is the uncovered class.

Observed live (2026-10-20 verification probing, free tier): a model returned a safety-refusal string as its entire apply response. It was packaged as a candidate and carried downstream before the structural gate rejected it. Final state was safe (no file written, honest terminal status) — the net held; this issue is about not relying on it for a detectable-at-intake class.

## Desired end state

- A cheap, deterministic intake screen for obvious non-candidate payloads (refusal phrasing, natural-language-only responses with no code/diff shape) runs alongside the existing empty/reasoning-only checks at `apply_policy.py:409-423`: screened responses are recorded as failed samples, the model is noted `ok=False`, and the lane rotates — same handling as the reasoning-only class.
- The missing-marker policy for genuinely code-shaped output stays exactly as documented in `prompts.py:209-211`.
- A missing-marker response no longer records model health `ok=True` unless the candidate it produced actually passes the downstream gates.

## Related

- #280 (calibration-driven first-rung selection + earlier rotation on structured-output failure) — this is the apply-path instance of the same structured-output-failure rotation theme; coordinate so the screening lives in one place.

## Estimate

~40 LoC + tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A refusal-string response is rotated at intake with health `ok=False`, never packaged as a candidate
- [ ] Code-shaped missing-marker responses behave exactly as before (tests pin this)
- [ ] Health/billable records for missing-marker responses reflect the candidate's actual downstream outcome
- [ ] Full suite + audit green

## Problem

In `driver_core` — the package's most safety-sensitive module — the `check_batch` docstring states a guarantee the implementation does not enforce. Anyone (or any future lane) trusting the documented contract gets weaker protection than documented.

Found during the 2026-10-20 full verification pass on main `dd83caf9`.

## Evidence (verified live)

- `driver_core/actions.py:253-258` — `check_batch` docstring: "Refuses a batch that mixes an irreversible action with anything else."
- `driver_core/actions.py:262-269` — the implementation only refuses **more than one** irreversible action in the batch.
- Live proof on `dd83caf9`: `check_batch(["delete_file", "observe"], v)` returned the batch **unchanged** — an irreversible action mixed with another action was accepted, contradicting the docstring.

Per-step irreversible consent is enforced separately in `driver_core/executor.py:331-336`, and `Driver.step` takes one decision per step — which is why the impact is low today. The risk is the documented contract being relied on when a batch path is wired up later (see #270-#273).

## Problem

The GUI server's POST handler reads the entire request body into memory with no size limit. On a `ThreadingHTTPServer`, concurrent oversized bodies multiply memory use; a token holder (or any local process, if the token ever leaks) can force the server to buffer and JSON-parse arbitrarily large payloads.

Found during the 2026-10-20 full verification pass on main `dd83caf9`.

## Evidence (verified live)

- `harness/server.py:1303-1304` — `n = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)` followed by `body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(n) ...)`: the full declared body is read with **no maximum**.
- Repro: `curl -X POST -H "X-Harness-Auth: <token>" --data-binary @<64MB JSON file> /api/chat` → the server read and parsed all 64MB in ~0.5s and rejected only on field validation (`"'prompt' is required"`, HTTP 400). A 6MB body behaved identically. Expected: reject oversized bodies with HTTP 413 **before** reading.
- `harness/server.py:1856` — `UiServer` is a `ThreadingHTTPServer`, so concurrent oversized POSTs multiply the buffered memory.

Mitigating context (why this is low severity, not critical): the bind is loopback-only with a FATAL exit for non-loopback hosts (`harness/server.py:1905`), and the auth guard (`harness/server.py:1300`) runs **before** the body read, so an unauthenticated remote cannot reach it. Practical exposure: a token holder or a local process.

## Desired end state

- `do_POST` rejects any request whose declared `Content-Length` exceeds a sane cap (suggested 1 MB — the largest legitimate API payload is far smaller) with HTTP 413, before any bytes are read.
- Behavior is identical for all POST routes (the check lives at the single read site, `harness/server.py:1303-1304`).
- A regression test posts an over-cap body and asserts 413 + the handler never parsed it; existing server tests stay green.

## Estimate

~15 LoC + one test.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Over-cap POST returns 413 without the body being read/parsed
- [ ] Normal-size POSTs (chat, driver, apply routes) unaffected
- [ ] Regression test lands with the fix; full suite + audit green

## Reconciliation evidence — 2026-10-30

This issue already covers the scope gap: its problem and acceptance name bare-`python` gate failures. I am recording the new evidence here instead of filing a duplicate.

### Current main and CI

At `0780ea7473e761638c75d12d20670264d7781916`, the exact CI unittest command, `python -W error::ResourceWarning -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, completed **5,168 tests, 72 skipped, exit 0** on Windows with Python 3.14.6 available on `PATH`. The exact-SHA CI check-runs completed with **14 successes and 1 skip, no failures**. The hermetic workflow installs Python through `actions/setup-python` and runs the same command ([workflow at this SHA](https://github.com/Sovereign-Communication/harness/blob/0780ea7473e761638c75d12d20670264d7781916/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L157-L185)).

### Earlier local failure

The 2026-10-29 status on [draft PR #442](https://github.com/Sovereign-Communication/harness/pull/442) records the prior full-suite run at then-main `ffeb4d2aa05f3153d052aa64ceb141fd7c7fd255`: 5,163 tests, exit 1, six failures in `test_declarations.OsBoundaryTests` (2), `test_tier_chain.OsalInputTests` (2), `test_wiring.LaunchDiagnosticTests` (1), and `test_osal.OsalUiTest.test_which_finds_the_running_interpreter` (1). The affected test/source files are unchanged between that SHA and current main.

The six PATH-dependent assertions represented by those class counts in current source are:

- `test_a_non_zero_exit_is_an_answer_not_a_failure`
- `test_a_command_that_actually_runs_returns_its_output`
- `test_a_child_really_receives_stdin`
- `test_a_child_that_ignores_stdin_still_works`
- `test_a_timeout_is_not_dressed_up_as_a_missing_binary`
- `test_which_finds_the_running_interpreter`

The prior status attributes the failure to invoking a virtual-environment interpreter by absolute path while its basename is not resolvable on `PATH`; CI's `setup-python` supplies a PATH-resolvable interpreter. On this Windows host, deliberately removing Python from `PATH` and rerunning those six tests reproduced the direct lookup failure in `test_which_finds_the_running_interpreter`; five bare-`python` subprocess tests passed because Windows process search resolves them differently. I therefore do not claim a six-failure reproduction on this Windows host or a current-main test failure.

### Disposition and gates

This is an environment-scope finding already tracked by #290. Current main and its exact-SHA CI run pass under the CI environment, and the earlier discrepancy is explained by the PATH precondition. No source change or CI scope change is indicated by this evidence; #290 remains open for its runbook acceptance.

Lucas Gate v2 deterministic validation: `pass`; category 9 is not applicable because the private Lucas profile is unavailable. No private-profile or typed voice-suite pass is claimed.

Jev direct System One call (`jev-latest`, resolved model `jev-1.14.0`, 1,145 input / 85 output tokens): disposition `proceed` (lead 0.66), `is_destructive=0.03`, `advances_goal=0.76`. The below-0.95 advances signal required investigation. Claim-level review of the current suite, exact-SHA CI results, PATH-dependent tests, and this issue's existing scope found no actual risk; proceed with this note under Jev Gate Policy v1 rule 6. No generic envelope PASS is claimed.

## Current-main reproduction — 2026-10-31

**Source and isolation**
- Archived exact fetched origin/main SHA 0780ea7473e761638c75d12d20670264d7781916; archive SHA256 C4E716345A41720B0BB021CF001259664F83BF0813CABF28A10EA18A5B8F8B48. The suite ran in a disposable extraction of that archive. The canonical lane checkout was not changed.
- Local Windows run used Python 3.14.6 from a fresh venv by absolute path, with PATH entries containing python.exe removed and credential-like environment variables cleared. The exact workflow command was: python -W error::ResourceWarning -m unittest discover -s tests -v.

**Reproduction**
- Exit 1: 5,168 tests, 1 failure, 74 skipped.
- The sole failing test was test_osal.OsalUiTest.test_which_finds_the_running_interpreter, with AssertionError: unexpectedly None. An explicit probe returned None for osal.which(basename(sys.executable)) when the venv interpreter was absent from PATH.
- With the venv Scripts directory restored to PATH, the affected OS-boundary classes plus interpreter-discovery test passed 21/21.

**CI scope**
- Exact-main GitHub Actions run 40938737769 at the same SHA completed successfully; all five hermetic matrix jobs passed (Ubuntu latest Python 3.11 and 3.13, Ubuntu 22.04 Python 3.9, macOS latest Python 3.11, Windows latest Python 3.11).
- Matching Windows job 123676187490 ran actions/setup-python and the same test command: 5,168 tests in 321.282s, OK with 48 skipped.
- Oct 28 workflow runs 40788849825 and 40789791504 also had all hermetic jobs successful. Their failing jobs were changed-file typecheck and audit, not the hermetic suite.
- The retained Oct 28 sandbox record at ffeb4d2 lists six PATH-sensitive OS-boundary failures, but does not retain the original platform or raw log. This Windows current-main replay reproduces the interpreter-lookup failure only; the other five are not claimed as reproduced. WSL/Linux is unavailable on this host.

**Disposition**
The observed failure is a local environment-scope difference: osal.which correctly returns None when the active interpreter is not PATH-resolvable, while CI uses setup-python before running the suite. No source fix is justified by this result. Existing issue #290 already covers bare-Python/environment failures and its canonical plan says not to file a duplicate; the Python 3.14 matrix omission is separately tracked by #443.

**Gates**
- Lucas Gate v2 passed first for this evidence; category 5 only, artifact SHA256 66cf2b1f82f32d85ecbbb77770cfaf91dca8f4c8f83c1dfed43aa793b411373d. No private-profile or voice claim is made.
- Direct TypeSafe System One P2 POST: HTTP 200, requested jev-latest, observed jev-1.14.0, usage 1,029 input / 86 output tokens. advances_goal=0.88 (below 0.95), is_destructive=0.08; disposition proceed (confidence 0.91; proceed 0.94, needs_improvement 0.05, escalate 0.01). I investigated the below-bar goal score against the exact archive, PATH probe, 21/21 rerun, exact-SHA CI matrix, and missing historical platform/log; no product or CI risk surfaced. This is not a generic Jev pass. P6 was not applicable because no implementation was made.

Operator-commissioned dossier (Lucas, 2026-10-19): Freebuff's desktop mission mode reverse-engineered from the shipped app so Hourglass can absorb its lessons and match its capabilities. Full text below; also saved on the operator box at `~/workspace/freebuff-re/freebuff-mission-dossier.md`, evidence in `~/workspace/freebuff-re/desktop/` + `~/workspace/freebuff-re/modules/`.

---

# Dossier — Freebuff "Mission" Mode, Reverse-Engineered from the Shipped Product

**Purpose:** give the harness lane everything verified about Freebuff's
mission feature so Hourglass (harness's mission/driver system) can absorb
its lessons and match its capabilities. Prepared 2026-10-19 by the
operator's agent from primary sources, at Lucas's direction.

**Provenance & confidence.** Everything in §1–§3 is read from the shipped
Freebuff Desktop build itself: Linux AppImage downloaded from
freebuff.com (`/api/desktop/download/linux-appimage`), desktop app
v0.0.182 (Electron), agent runtime in `resources/orchestrator/orchestrator.js`
(11 MB Bun bundle, module paths preserved). Key modules:
`src/shared/mission-prompt.ts`, `src/shared/mission.ts`,
`src/server/services/mission.ts`. The CLI was also analyzed (npm
`freebuff` 0.2.30, binary checksum-verified against the package manifest):
**the CLI has no mission mode at all** — the feature exists only in the
desktop GUI. Public documentation: none exists (official blog/docs/repos,
Reddit, X, Product Hunt, YouTube, changelog mirrors all searched —
nothing names or describes it). Metering facts in §4 marked
"owner-confirmed" come from Lucas's account, not the code.

---

## 1. What the feature actually is

Mission mode is a **manager/worker loop inside one desktop tab**:

- The **worker** is the ordinary coding agent in the tab. Passes run in
  the **same conversation** — context accumulates across passes; there
  are no fresh sessions. (The common description "the model writes its
  own next prompt and hands it to a fresh session" is wrong in the
  session detail; what's fresh each round is the manager's *decision*.)
- The **manager** is a separate agent, **Buffy** (hosted agent id
  `freebuff-desktop-autorun`; system prompt begins "You are Buffy, the
  auto-run agent behind Freebuff Desktop. You decide what one tab does
  next."). Buffy **never reads files, edits code, runs commands, or sees
  code**. It runs before the first pass and after every coding turn, and
  must emit exactly one decision (a `decide` tool call, or one JSON
  object on the non-hosted backends):
  `{read, decision: "run"|"stop", why, input: {skill | label+prompt,
  purpose: "required"|"refinement"}, declined[], expectedGain,
  confidence, evidence[]}`.
  `expectedGain` is a 0–3 forecast of improvement to the final outcome's
  0–10 correctness/quality **geometric mean**; `declined[]` records
  candidate actions Buffy considered and rejected.
- The user's mission text **governs the thread and wins over defaults**;
  it is quoted verbatim at the end of Buffy's system prompt.

## 2. The trace (what the manager sees — "bones")

Buffy decides from a clipped trace, never the raw conversation:

- Agent prose clipped to **4,000 chars** per message; each tool call
  rendered as **one line, 140 chars**; diff summaries as file-count
  lines; subagent activity as summary lines.
- The **original user request is the scope anchor** (≤8,000 chars) and is
  preserved when the trace exceeds **60,000 chars** — earlier turns are
  dropped with an "earlier turns omitted" marker and the recent trace is
  kept.
- **Receipts** per pass: manager vs worker tokens, cost, duration. The
  last **8** passes' receipts are shown to Buffy so it can judge whether
  passes are getting more or less efficient.

## 3. Steering machinery

- **Quality model:** four dimensions — **Spec, Design, Correctness,
  Concision/Quality** — climbed as a ladder in that order. In the
  **writer regime (effort ≤3)**, every worker pass must begin its report
  with `GRADES spec=<n> design=<n> correctness=<n> quality=<n>;
  biggest gap: ...` and Buffy steers at the **lowest** grade, choosing
  targets anchored to skill bodies. In the **catalog regime
  (effort 4–5)**, Buffy picks from the action/skill catalog.
- **Effort slider 1–5 → time budgets 15 / 30 / 60 / 120 / 240 minutes**
  (`MISSION_TIME_BUDGET_MINUTES`; default effort **3** = 60 min).
  The budget is a **target, not a cutoff**: required work runs past it;
  per `MISSION_COMPLETION_GUIDANCE`, the loop stops only when the
  requested outcomes exist **and are verified**, or on a concrete
  blocker that needs user input.
- **Delivery gating:** catalog actions **commit / push / open-pr /
  merge-pr / merge-local** (plus review, test, brainstorm, derisk) may
  be chosen **only when the mission text asks for them**. Nothing in
  Buffy's own prompt authorizes a delivery step.
- **Mission text constraints:** hard cap **4,000 chars**
  (`MAX_MISSION_PROMPT_CHARS`; `normalizeMissionPrompt` truncates).
  At most **12** saved missions. Presets: **Explore** (investigate,
  edit nothing), **Commit** (work + local commit, never push),
  **Merge PR** (default prompt: "Complete the user's request fully.
  When the work is correct, lean, and verified, commit it, open a
  pull request, drive its checks to green, and merge it.").
- **Decider backends (3):** (a) hosted Freebuff autorun agent —
  stateful via `previousRun`, only tool is `decide`,
  `maxAgentSteps 2`; (b) **Claude Code** — resumed session, JSON
  output; (c) **Codex** — resumed thread, `sandboxMode: read-only`,
  `networkAccessEnabled: false`, `approvalPolicy: "never"`. Decider
  state is carried per thread (sessionId/threadId); only new message
  segments are sent after the first decision.
- **Reliability:** 120 s timeout per decision attempt
  (`MISSION_RETRY_POLICY timeoutMs: 120000`), retries after 15 s and
  45 s, one re-ask with a nudge on an unusable answer. Failures are
  classified **blocked / unreachable / unusable** with user-facing
  notes (e.g. "Mission couldn't get a decision… Send a message to
  pick it back up." / "…the tab is yours again.").
- A project-understanding agent runs on `openai/gpt-6-luna` (1M ctx).
- The CLI framework separately has `spawn_agents` /
  `spawn_agent_inline` (fresh runs with `ancestorRunIds` lineage and
  filtered history) — a different mechanism; the desktop mission does
  not use it.

## 4. Metering context (owner-confirmed unless noted)

- Pools are **fully separate**: sessions on the connected ChatGPT
  account burn **only** Codex usage (5-hour + weekly windows,
  account-shared across all Codex surfaces), **zero Freebucks**;
  Freebuff-native models burn only Freebucks.
- Freebuff-native **Luna = 20 Freebucks/hour**; Lucas's $8/mo plan
  shows **250 Freebucks/day** (≈12.5 Luna-hours/day). Public README
  corroborates the unit economics: since 2026-10-15, **1 hour =
  5 Freebucks**, balances read in hours.
- **Freebuff sessions hard-end at 1 hour; tokens inside the hour are
  unmetered** (owner-confirmed). Codex `/status` shows 5h % left,
  weekly % left, exact reset timestamps, credits, and banked resets;
  values go stale (>15 min → send a message to refresh). Banked
  "full" resets restore **both** windows and expire unreplaced.
- **Auto-redeem of banked resets does NOT exist in this build** —
  zero hits for redeem/banked/autoRedeem/usageReset across the
  orchestrator bundle, the UI chunk, and the Electron main code.

## 5. Lessons for Hourglass / HUL — integration map

HUL (jev-roadmap Track B) already has the mission pack (HUL-A), dual
budget (HUL-B), Jev scope gate (HUL-C), and until-limits driver
(HUL-D). Freebuff's shipped design validates that architecture and
adds concrete, battle-tested details worth absorbing:

| # | Freebuff mechanism | Hourglass/HUL integration |
|---|---|---|
| L1 | Manager sees a **clipped trace only** (4,000-char prose, 140-char tool lines, 60,000-char budget, scope anchor preserved) | Adopt the trace spec as the default context packet for any HUL decider/judge step. It is a proven budget for "enough to decide, never enough to drown." |
| L2 | **Typed decision object** with `expectedGain` forecast, `confidence`, `evidence[]`, `declined[]` | Mirror this schema in the HUL driver's step decisions and in Hourglass supervision: every continue/stop carries a forecast, evidence, and the rejected alternatives — auditable by construction. |
| L3 | **Self-grade line** (`GRADES spec/design/correctness/quality`) + steer-at-the-lowest + ladder order | Adopt as the pass-report header for HUL attempts; the driver routes the next attempt at the weakest dimension instead of re-asking "what next?" from scratch. |
| L4 | **Effort → time-target** mapping; target ≠ cutoff; stop only on verified outcomes or a concrete user-input blocker | HUL already runs until limits/stall; add Buffy's completion rule verbatim in spirit: "feels done" and "budget reached" are both non-reasons to stop while required work remains. |
| L5 | **Delivery actions gated by the mission text** itself | Aligns with HUL-C scope packs: the mission pack should enumerate permitted delivery actions; the driver refuses catalog actions the pack didn't grant. |
| L6 | **Decider reliability**: 120 s timeout, 15 s/45 s retries, one re-ask, blocked/unreachable/unusable taxonomy, graceful "tab is yours again" fallback | Port the taxonomy + retry shape into the Hourglass supervisor so a dead decider degrades to a parked, journaled lane — never a spinning one. |
| L7 | **Receipts split manager vs worker** tokens/cost/duration, last-8 window shown to the decider | Split HUL receipts the same way (driver/judge spend vs attempt spend); feed the recent window into stall detection. |
| L8 | Stop decisions are **self-assessed by the manager** (no external typed gate) | **Gap in Freebuff that HUL already closes**: keep HUL-C's Jev scope gate as the authority on "complete" — do not regress to manager self-assessment. Hourglass's edge over the shipped product is precisely this gate. |
| L9 | **No cross-session handoff**: the mission lives and dies in one tab/conversation | **Second gap HUL already closes**: the mission pack + resume pack (HUL-A/D) survive process death; keep positioning Hourglass as the durable form of the same loop. |
| L10 | **4,000-char mission cap** with silent truncation | Any Hourglass-generated mission text destined for Freebuff must be ≤4,000 chars, steering-complete, and point the worker at a repo-resident constitution (pattern already landed: SCMessenger PR #617 `docs/roles/MISSION-PROMPT.md` Part 0 paste text ≈2,950 chars + burst variant). Add a length check to the generator. |
| L11 | **No auto-redeem, no mission API** — redemption and GUI supervision cannot be product features | They are Hourglass driver features (issues #270–273 line): wall watch, `/status` reads, stall pick-up messages, armed-threshold "Use reset" clicks, and pop-up adjudication. The decision protocol specced in SCMessenger PR #617 `docs/roles/DUAL-ENGINE-24-7.md` (Class 1 mechanical / Class 2 Jev-judged at ≥0.95 from a context packet / Class 3 never-the-driver's) is the reference spec. |
| L12 | **Work allocation by metering axis** (also PR #617): token-metered/unlimited-time engine takes slow, sleep-heavy, judgment work; time-metered/unmetered-token engine takes pre-staged 60-minute execution bursts with a reserved handoff window | Hourglass scheduling should classify work items by token density × decision density and route accordingly when it drives mixed Freebuff/Codex lanes. |

## 6. Suggested lane actions

1. Add an `HG`/`HUL-E` item to jev-roadmap adopting L1–L3 (trace
   spec, decision schema, grade-line protocol) into the HUL driver;
   hermetic tests against recorded decision fixtures (~250–400 LoC).
2. Add the L10 length check + Part-0-style pointer pattern to any
   Freebuff mission-text generation path (~30 LoC + test).
3. Wire L11's decision classes into the driver-core work in
   #270–273 (vision verification ≥0.85 already specced there;
   Class 2 raises the bar to ≥0.95 for judgment clicks).
4. Keep L8/L9 as stated non-goals for parity work: HUL's Jev gate
   and durable mission pack are ahead of the shipped product;
   parity must not dilute them.

## 7. Evidence index

- Extracted modules + AppImage on the operator box:
  `~/workspace/freebuff-re/desktop/` (AppImage, `squashfs-root/`,
  `app-extracted/`), `~/workspace/freebuff-re/modules/` (mission
  modules), `~/workspace/freebuff-re/` (CLI tarball + strings).
- CLI binary authenticity: archive sha256 matches npm
  `binaryChecksums.linux-x64` exactly.
- Companion specs (SCMessenger PR #617, branch
  `docs/permanent-roles`): `docs/roles/MISSION-PROMPT.md` (v2),
  `docs/roles/DUAL-ENGINE-24-7.md` (allocation doctrine +
  decision escalation protocol).
- Harness canon referenced: `docs/jev-roadmap.md` (HUL track),
  `docs/harness-mission-until-limits.md` (pointer),
  `docs/hourglass-vision.md`, issues #270–273.

S4 RE-SCOPE DISPOSITION - RECORDED FIRST, per the owner steering (2026-11-01; recorded on this issue 2026-11-02 at the owner's direction)

The NL endpoint is deferred with #271. This slice wires STRUCTURED launch plans instead: a launch plan is the manifest's declared step list, executed through driver_step under the consent model below.

CONSENT: assignment-bound - a gate-passed queue item pre-authorizes its declared mutating steps, bound to the item's plan hash, single-use, expiring. Read-only steps are free. Irreversible actions (delete_file, submit_irreversible) are excluded from launch plans entirely, and the vocabulary check refuses them.

PRE-LAUNCH CHECKLIST, fail-closed - any failure aborts before paste and parks the item with the failed check named: no STOP on the item or its tracker; lane lock free; budget covers one full session block; vision gate (S3, #272) passes on the setup screenshot.

EXECUTION: events stream through the existing driver_step_* events; cancel stops remaining steps. Acceptance is TM3: one real queue item launched under the frozen protocol, post-launch vision confirms the running state (start_state field, post-launch form), receipts recorded. S3 SPEC - VISION VERIFICATION, THE SPECIFIC JEV GATE (owner steering, 2026-11-01; recorded on this issue 2026-11-02 at the owner's direction)

Implement a versioned vision gate pack (working name: launch-verify pack v1) in the Jev pack owner - no second Jev client. Vision plumbing already exists in driver_core/extractors.py (VisionExtractor, screenshot as sole asset, PNG-only, omit-don't-guess); this slice builds the gate on it.

PER FIELD, TWO QUESTIONS over the same screenshot: (a) a Choice extraction naming the visibly selected value from the field's declared option set (including not_visible), which CODE compares to the manifest value; (b) a Score 0-3 match question with concrete level criteria (0 = row absent or value clearly differs; 1 = row visible, value unreadable or ambiguous; 2 = value readable and matching but partially obscured or low-contrast; 3 = value clearly readable and exactly matching), mapped to percent as score/3 x 100. A field passes only when extraction agrees with the manifest AND its score meets the bar.

FIELDS: app_identity (FreeBuff Desktop is the foreground app); backend (FreeBuff | Codex); model (exact string from the manifest's declared option list); thinking (the manifest's effort/thinking level); repo (tab repo matches the manifest checkout); build_mode (build mode active, plan loaded); mission_queued (the item's mission present in the queue); start_state (pre-launch: Start control present, no session already running; post-launch, in S4: running indicator present).

COMPOSITION AND BARS: per-field minimum - the lowest field governs. The floor bar is 95 for every field. Calibration may RAISE a field's bar on corpus evidence (backend and model are the candidates); no field's bar ever goes below 95. Calibration runs use two independent vision slots (the extractor pool's independence rules forbid shared answers). Screenshots: PNG via ScreenSource, prepared through the existing image pipeline; capture the launch panel region when the full screen scores in level 2 territory for readability reasons.

ITERATE UNTIL PERFECT (owner rule): a below-bar field starts diagnosis, never a bar change and never an unchanged re-roll. Classify the driver: (1) wrong selection actually on screen - correct the selection, re-shoot; (2) readability (occlusion, scaling, contrast, wrong region) - fix the capture (focus, maximize, panel crop), re-run; (3) gate ambiguity (extraction and score disagree, or the option set / level criteria do not separate real cases) - sharpen THAT field in the pack (declared options, level wording, crop region), bump the pack version, record the change with before/after scores on the calibration corpus. Loop until a true no-note pass: every field at or above bar with extraction agreement. Three consecutive stalled rounds - stop and report scores plus the failing field's evidence. A pass-with-note does not close any item.

CALIBRATION CORPUS (build before live calibration): real screenshots from the installed FreeBuff - setup panel default; Codex selected; FreeBuff selected; each selectable model; each thinking level; build mode with plan loaded; mission queued; session running - plus one negative variant per field (that field wrong, everything else correct). The corpus is the regression set for every pack change: a pack revision must pass the full corpus, not just the case that failed.

FREEZE: the first fully passing live run is the calibration run. Freeze the protocol (step sequence, declared targets, pack version, per-field bars, expected values shape) with its receipts, following the repo's existing freeze pattern. Any later change to steps, targets, pack, or FreeBuff version breaks the freeze and requires a new calibration run against the corpus first.

Prototype evidence (overseer-run, 2026-11-01, synthetic setup screenshots, jev-1.14.0): a correct setup scored 99.3-99.7 per field and passed; a wrong-model variant was caught (extraction read the wrong model, match score 0.3, gate failed). Full fast-track record: PR #442.

## Problem
The driver_core vocabulary has no way to launch an application. `type_text`, `click`, `focus` exist, but nothing opens a program. This blocks "control my computer" scenarios.

## End state
`driver_core` can launch a declared application by name via a new `launch_app` action.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `Action("launch_app", MUTATING, "launch_app", ("app_name",), ...)` added to `_declare()` in `driver_core/actions.py`
- [ ] `execute_launch_app(app_name: str)` in `driver_core/executor.py` with OS dispatch:
  - Windows: `subprocess.Popen(["cmd", "/c", "start", "", app_exe])`
  - macOS: `subprocess.Popen(["open", "-a", app_name])`
  - Linux: `subprocess.Popen(["xdg-open", app_desktop])`
